title: Who is the best performer over four games?
description: A table gives the points three players scored in four games, and one player missed a game. The mean points per game are found by dividing each total by the games actually played, and the means are compared.
teaching_notes: One idea: divide a total by the number of values that were really recorded. Watch for children who count a game not played as a zero, or who drop a real zero.

video_script.why: The child can find a mean and now handles a zero and a missing game.
video_script.substitution: A game not played gives no score, but a zero is a game played badly.
video_script.anchor: A table of points in four games: first player 14, 16, 10, 10; second player 0, 8, 6, 4; third player 8, 11, did not play, 13
video_script.payoff_line: The first player is the best performer.

final_answer.spoken: the first player is the best performer

maths_rules: second player played all four; 0 is a real score: 0 + 8 + 6 + 4 = 18; 18 ÷ 4 = 4.5
highest mean 12.5, so the first player is the best performer
video_script.design: One table of points. Each player's row gets its total and its count of games played.
open_questions: The book labels the players A, B and C; the script says first, second and third player so that no letter has to be spoken.

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m3: the did not play cell glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A table shows the points scored by three players in four games.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The third player did not play one game.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How should each average be found, and who is the best performer?

beats.on_screen: the table stays on the board

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: total ÷ games played; a game not played is crossed out of the count; a zero stays in the count

marks.m1: total ÷ games played is written and labelled mean
marks.m2: the not played cell is crossed out of the count
marks.m3: a zero stays in the count
marks.m4: the hint line the same way as the book's example glows

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The total divided by the number of games played is called the mean.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A game that was not played is not counted.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A score of zero is counted, because the game was played.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>We solve it the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Given: first player 14, 16, 10, 10; second player 0, 8, 6, 4; third player 8, 11, (did not play), 13

marks.m1: the first player's row is written
marks.m2: the second player's row is written
marks.m3: the third player's row is written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the first player scored fourteen, sixteen, ten and ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The second player scored zero, eight, six and four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The third player scored eight, eleven and thirteen, and did not play one game.

beats.on_screen: To find: mean points per game of each player; the best performer

marks.m1: the two questions are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find each player's mean points per game, and the best performer.

marks.m2: the total 50 and the count 4 are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, find the mean for the first player. Add fourteen, sixteen, ten and ten to get fifty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>All four games were played, so divide by four.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Fifty divided by four is twelve point five points per game.

marks.m1: the not played cell is crossed out of the count

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, find the mean for the third player. One game was not played, so only three games are counted.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Divide by three, not four. Eight, eleven and thirteen add up to thirty two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Thirty two divided by three is about ten point six seven.

marks.m1: the zero is circled and kept in the count

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, find the mean for the second player. All four games were played, so divide by four.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The zero is a real score, so it stays. Zero, eight, six and four add up to eighteen.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Eighteen divided by four is four point five.

beats.on_screen: means: 12.5, 10.67 and 4.5; the greatest mean marks the best performer

marks.m1: the three means are written side by side

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, compare the three means. The player with the greatest mean performs best.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twelve point five is greater than ten point six seven and four point five.

marks.m1: each mean is multiplied back by its number of games

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step five, check each mean by multiplying it back by its number of games. Twelve point five times four is fifty.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Four point five times four is eighteen. Ten point six seven times three is about thirty two.

beats.on_screen: Answer: first player 12.5 points per game; third player (divide by 3) ≈ 10.67; second player (divide by 4) = 4.5; the first player is the best performer
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The first player is the best performer.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The mean is twelve point five points per game.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The third player's mean is about ten point six seven, found by dividing by three. The second player's mean is four point five, found by dividing by four.
